column1: # The law of the game: who counts as the authority where, and what killing costs. The owner edits this file; the game reads it
# when it is built. Columns are separated by tabs. Lines starting with # are notes. Every value here is a PLACEHOLDER until the owner
# has said, except where a line says it was asked for (7 Nov 2026).
#   hear_metres      how far a crime is heard, through walls
#   call_metres      how far an authority that sees a crime calls its mates and a civilian calls the nearest authority
#   calm_seconds     how long after the last crime the authorities that saw it stay hostile when the criminal is out of their sight
#   call_far_metres  how far a civilian's call for the nearest authority reaches
#   flee_seconds     how long a civilian who saw a crime runs
#   shut_from        the wanted level (1 to 3) from which shops close and ordinary talk is refused
#   neutral         armed or a guard, not hostile and not plot
#   fleeing         a hostile that is running away or has surrendered
#   hostile         whoever attacks the player anyway
# (7 Nov: civilian -10, friendly or neutral non-plot -5, hostile 0, surrendered or fleeing hostile -2; a plot creature cannot be hit)
# authority <module prefix> <part of a creature's template name>
#   A creature of a module whose name starts with the prefix and whose template contains the text is an authority there.
#   The factions of the game's creatures are only Neutral, Friendly, Hostile and the like, so the templates tell them apart.
#   First guesses from the module survey (`cargo run -p kotor-game --example law_survey`) and the owner's list:
#   Taris: Sith patrols, Tatooine: Czerka and the Sandral guard, Dantooine: Jedi and militia, Manaan: Selkath,
#   Kashyyyk: Wookiee defenders, Korriban: Sith students and the port authority, Endar Spire and the Leviathan: Sith and Republic soldiers.
